observation_summary: The optimizer fails to respect custom convergence criteria, leading to incorrect or unexpected optimization results when compared to expected theoretical values.
reasoning_summary: The LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer was designed to support a custom VectorialConvergenceChecker, but the implementation completely ignored this parameter during the optimization loop. Instead, it relied exclusively on hardcoded internal convergence parameters (cost and parameter relative tolerances). The fix involved modifying the optimization loop to check if a custom checker is provided; if so, it uses that checker to determine convergence, otherwise it falls back to the default internal logic. This ensures that users can define custom stopping criteria as intended by the API.
